newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq says indices jumped double-digits in Q2.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq says indices jumped double-digits in Q2.

text.p: Nasdaq said its indices rose sharply in the second quarter, with all posting double-digit gains except the Nasdaq Biotechnology Index .IXB.

The Nasdaq Composite .IXIC rose 18.0 percent for the quarter to 1442.07, the Nasdaq Stock Market said in a press release. The best performing index was the Nasdaq Telecommunications Index .IXUT, which surged 23.2 percent. Close behind was a 21.7 percent rise in the Nasdaq Computer Index .IXK.
Share volume edged down 1.7 percent, averaging 592.8 million shares, down from 602.9 million in the same quarter last year, Nasdaq said.

Dollar volume rose 15.1 percent to $16 billion a day, from $13.9 billion. For the quarter, dollar volume hit $1.027 billion, the highest amount ever, beating the previous record of $997 billion set in the first quarter of 1997.
The market value of the more than 5,530 Nasdaq listed companies hit $1.68 trillion, up 10.8 percent from the end of 1996.
Nasdaq said its share volume exceeded that of its rival, the New York Stock Exchange, every trading day of 1997.
